name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for one week first. This gives us real-world data on false positives and gaps without slowing teams down. The trade-off is delayed immediate feedback, but we avoid disrupting workflows while building confidence in the tool’s accuracy. After the week, we’ll decide whether to switch to parallel review mode based on the error rate and team feedback.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode normalizes PR-Agent noise—reviewers learn to ignore *all* comments, including real risks. False negatives (missed issues) are the real danger, and shadow mode won’t catch them. Instead, run PR-Agent on a *random 10% of PRs* for a week, then compare its missed issues against manual reviews. If the gap is small, expand; if not, scrap it.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for two weeks first. This gives us the broadest baseline to measure false positives and false negatives across the entire codebase. The trade-off is delayed immediate feedback for some teams, but we avoid skewing data by cherry-picking PRs. After the two weeks, we’ll have real-world metrics to decide whether to expand, adjust, or cut the experiment.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for two weeks, then switch to random 10% parallel review for one week to compare missed issues against manual review.

Result: A data-backed confidence score for PR-Agent’s accuracy, with false positives and false negatives quantified. Owned by Overhaul.
